title: Job 3
paragraphs: ¹ After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth. ² He said: ³ "May the day I was born be destroyed, and the night it was announced, 'A boy is conceived.' ⁴ May that day be darkness — may God above not seek it out, nor any light shine on it. ⁵ May darkness and deep shadow claim it; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm its light.

⁶ As for that night — may thick darkness seize it; may it not be included among the days of the year or counted among the months. ⁷ May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it. ⁸ May those who curse the day curse it — those skilled at rousing Leviathan. ⁹ May its morning stars turn dark; may it wait in vain for the light of dawn, never seeing the first rays of sunrise — ¹⁰ because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb and hide trouble from my eyes.

¹¹ Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not perish as I came from the womb? ¹² Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts to nurse me? ¹³ If only I had never come into being, or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave. ¹⁴ I would now be lying in peaceful sleep, at rest with kings and rulers of the earth who built themselves places now lying in ruins, ¹⁵ or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

¹⁶ Or why was I not buried like a stillborn child — like an infant who never saw the light of day? ¹⁷ There the wicked cease their troubling, and there the weary find rest. ¹⁸ There the prisoners rest together, no longer hearing the voice of the oppressor. ¹⁹ The small and the great are there alike, and the slave is free from his master. ²⁰ Why is light given to those who are in misery, and life to the bitter in soul,

²¹ who long for death that does not come, and search for it more eagerly than for hidden treasure? ²² How glad they would be, how they would rejoice, to reach the grave at last! ²³ Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in? ²⁴ For my groaning comes before I eat; my anguish pours out like water. ²⁵ What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has overtaken me.
²⁶ I have no peace, no quietness; I have no rest — only turmoil.
